source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 2 (Rights in the Indian Constitution).

sections.heading: 1. Fundamental Rights — Overview
points: **Fundamental Rights (Part III)** are the basic rights guaranteed to citizens, enforceable by courts (justiciable); inspired by the US **Bill of Rights**.
They protect citizens against arbitrary state action; can be **suspended during a National Emergency** (except Articles 20 and 21).

sections.heading: 2. The Six Fundamental Rights
points: **Right to Equality (Art 14–18)** — equality before law, no discrimination, abolition of untouchability and titles.
**Right to Freedom (Art 19–22)** — speech/expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession; protection in respect of conviction (Art 20) and life & liberty (Art 21).
**Right against Exploitation (Art 23–24)** — bans human trafficking, forced labour, child labour.
**Right to Freedom of Religion (Art 25–28)** — freedom of conscience, practice, propagation.
**Cultural and Educational Rights (Art 29–30)** — protect minorities' language, script, culture, institutions.
**Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32)** — Dr Ambedkar called it the **'heart and soul' of the Constitution**; move courts (writs).

sections.heading: 3. Writs and Related Rights
points: **Five writs:** **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari** — issued by SC (Art 32) and HCs (Art 226).
**Right to Property** was removed as a Fundamental Right (44th Amendment, 1978) → now a legal right (Art 300A).
**Right to Education (Art 21A)** was added (86th Amendment, 2002) — free and compulsory education (6–14 years).

sections.heading: 4. Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties
points: **Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV)** — non-justiciable guidelines to the state for a welfare/just society (from Ireland).
**Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Art 51A)** — added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the recommendation of the **Swaran Singh Committee**; originally 10, now **11** duties.
Rights, Directives and Duties together aim at social justice.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Six Fundamental Rights (Part III); Right to Property removed by 44th Amendment (1978).
Art 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) = 'heart and soul' (Ambedkar).
Five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, Certiorari.
Directive Principles (Part IV) = non-justiciable (from Ireland).
Fundamental Duties added by 42nd Amendment (1976); Art 51A; now 11.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Right to Property is NO longer a Fundamental Right** (now a legal right, Art 300A).
**Art 32 = Right to Constitutional Remedies** = 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.
**Directive Principles are non-justiciable** (not enforceable in court).
**Fundamental Duties** were added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** — now 11.
